annotationRationale: Two independent tails return the game to the same state, allowing a first-step probability equation. Solving that linear equation gives the winning probability.
sourceMethod: Followed the first official method, which sets the winning probability equal to the immediate-win probability plus the contribution from restarting after two tails.

review.mathCheck: Two initial tails have probability (2/3)(3/5)=2/5 and restore Amelia's turn with unchanged future probabilities. Her disjoint winning cases give w=1/3+(2/5)w, hence w=5/9. The fraction is reduced, so q−p=4, choice D.
review.sourceMethodCheck: Faithful, independently worded adaptation of the first approach in MAA Solution 18 on page 6. It explains the reset state and disjoint cases before solving the same first-step equation.
review.annotationCheck: The recurrence, independence, and algebra annotations match the explanation. The recursion node includes combining disjoint transitions, so a separate probability-addition node is optional. No infinite-series node is needed.
